# Native temporal synthetic PG fixtures

The day/week/month compact JSON files are full owning `netshop_periods_v1` responses serialized by the actual dedicated reader in private PostgreSQL run `crossdomain-pg-07036f35d4b12b2f`, on main493 plus the dedicated author draft, then compared with final full run `crossdomain-pg-135167c15e045e12`. Sidecars record original request, typed7:3 header, source SHA/worktree dirty and owning code hashes. `registered-optin-series` and `registered-optin-max-series` retain original signed loopback HTTP response bytes captured in run `crossdomain-pg-aa949484936900f7` and compared to the final run. Maximum is four exact objects × two366-day windows, all2928 points retained, complete HTTP body441337 bytes. They are synthetic facts, not live or production receipts. The superseded uncompressed run e801c3 and 2693144-byte413 draft remain external historical evidence; they are not the compact version.

The two independent windows are Sep1–9 and Aug1–5. One trusted ERP order has product rows on Sep1 and Sep2, so daily counts are each1 but the calendar-week denominator is1, never2. An empty date bucket is null/no_records; Sep8 is an actual typed zero row with a missing trusted order number, so its per-order mean is unavailable. Costs and gross-profit proof remain unverified. A different shop appears in parent summary/full union, but is not silently added to the selected plot. Values, dates, metadata and identity scopes are not adjusted to make consumer tests pass.
